customManagers.description: v1/ansible compose templates (Jinja): literal image refs, digest-only refs, and Jinja default() pins, either as the tag or as the whole image reference

v2 plain-YAML app manifests, compose/swarm-compose files, and the 2 skfence Jinja compose templates: literal image refs (v2 has no Jinja default() image pins today; the one bash-style ${VERSION:-latest} reference in v2/apps/skfence is not extractable by this pattern and is called out in docs/dependency-updates.md)

packageRules.description: Group minor/patch/digest bumps per service directory (v1: the ansible role dir, v2: the app dir); majors are never grouped so each lands as its own reviewable PR
docker-mailserver majors need a human: prod was three majors behind what :latest resolved to before this framework started pinning (see test_skmail_dms_version_pinned.py)
postgres majors need a human: in-place major upgrades need a pg_upgrade/dump-restore step, never an unattended image swap

skmem-pg and the skdata stub stay on Postgres 17: the sovereign image is built from our own Dockerfile (pgvector + ParadeDB pg_search + Apache AGE) and no Postgres 18 build is published. Re-enable when a pg18 image exists.
Authentik (sksso) majors need a human: config/schema migrations between majors are not always backward compatible
Forgejo (skgit) majors need a human: git hosting is not something to auto-upgrade unattended
Nextcloud (skhub) majors need a human: app-store compatibility and data migrations across majors are not safe to automate

ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres is pinned to exactly what the pinned Immich release's docker-compose.yml names (Immich supports only that image and tag, and the PG major must never change silently); it moves only with an IMMICH_VERSION bump
mariadb tracks the newest LTS that Nextcloud supports (12.3, patch builds only); rolling majors such as 13.x are not supported by Nextcloud and are short-lived
